130	- **Never route an `error` port back into the happy path** — an error edge into the next happy-path node, or into the same End node the success path reaches, makes every failed run report `Completed` with success-shaped outputs. Send it to a distinct End node with an error/status output, to `core.logic.terminate`, or to a branch that genuinely recovers.
131	- **Never edit `content/*.bpmn`** — it is auto-generated from the `.flow` file and will be overwritten.
132	- **Never use `core.logic.mock` when the resource is in the same solution** — use `--local` discovery instead. Mock placeholders are only for resources that are not in the current solution and not yet published.
133	- **Never hand-write `definitions` entries** — always copy from registry output. Hand-written definitions have wrong port schemas and cause validation failures.
134	- **Never put any `model` block on node instances** — BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, binding templates, and context templates all live in the node's **definition** (copied verbatim from `registry get` into `definitions[]`). Instances carry only per-instance data: `inputs`, `outputs`, `display`. Identity fields like `entryPointId` / `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers) and `color` / `content` (sticky notes) live under `inputs`. This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source = <UUID>`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance.
135	- **Never author `model.context[]` on resource-node instances** — resource-node instances have no `model` block. For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition (from `registry get`) already carries `model.context[]` with `<bindings.{name}>` placeholders. Your job is to add matching entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array — two entries per resource node (`name` + `folderPath`) with `resourceKey` matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`. At BPMN emit, the runtime rewrites `<bindings.{name}>` → `=bindings.{id}` via `(resourceKey, name)` matching. Without the top-level `bindings[]` entries, `uip maestro flow validate` passes but `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder." See the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
136	- **Never put a `ui` block on node instances** — position and size belong in the top-level `layout.nodes` object. Nodes with `"ui": { "position": ... }` use the wrong format and may not render correctly in Studio Web.
137	- **Never skip `flow format` before publish or debug** — without it, hand-written `layout` data renders as misshapen rectangles in Studio Web (the MST-9061 failure mode). See rule #12 above for the format step.
138	- **Never validate after every individual edit** — intermediate flow states (e.g., node added but not yet wired) are expected to be invalid. Run `uip maestro flow validate` once after the full build is complete.
139	- **Never use `console.log` in script nodes** — `console` is not available in the Jint runtime. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
140	- **Never forget output mapping on End nodes** — every `out` variable in `variables.globals` must have a `source` expression in every reachable End node's `outputs`. Missing mappings cause silent runtime failures.
141	- **Never update `in` variables** — only `inout` variables can be modified via `variableUpdates`. Input variables are read-only after flow start.
142	- **Never reference parent-scope `$vars` inside a subflow** — subflows have isolated scope. Pass values explicitly via subflow inputs.
143	- **Never use `core.action.http` (v1)** — the v1 node is deprecated for all HTTP requests (both connector-authenticated and manual). For connector-auth, v1's `authenticationType: "connection"` input does not pass IS credentials at runtime. Use `core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request) for every HTTP node. See [http/planning.md](references/plugins/http/planning.md).
144	- **Never hand-write `definitions[]` or `inputs.*` for managed HTTP nodes** — use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for `branches` / `timeout` / `retryCount`) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths. Hand-written `definitions[]` strips required manifest fields; hand-written `inputs.detail` misses `essentialConfiguration` and fails at runtime. See [http/impl.md](references/plugins/http/impl.md).
145	- **Never write `$vars.X` (or `$metadata.X`, `$self.X`) without `=js:` in value fields** — `flow validate` flags this as MST-9107. See rule #11 above and [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the per-node-type field reference.
146	- **Never reuse a reference ID (mailbox folder, Slack channel, Jira project, Google Sheet, etc.) from a prior flow or session** — reference IDs are scoped to the specific authenticated account behind the connection. A `parentFolderId` from one Outlook mailbox is invalid in another; a Slack channel ID from one workspace is invalid in another. A reused ID passes `flow validate` and `node configure` cleanly, then faults silently at runtime with no resolvable error. Always re-resolve via `uip is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName> --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID> --output json` against the connection bound to this flow — do not paste a value you saw in another flow. See [connector/impl.md — Step 4](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) and [connector-trigger/impl.md — Step 3](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md).
147	- **Never include `[*]` literally in a connector `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key** — `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` is an array marker. Strip it and pass a `=js:` expression returning the array (e.g. `"fields.labels[*]"` → `"fields.labels": "=js:(['a', 'b'])"`). Never a literal JSON array — it validates but does not bind. 7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10

12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach

16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))
18	- The flow is a straightforward linear pipeline (trigger → action → action → end)

33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
44	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:end-->
45	
46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so you set the solution name yourself rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The solution and project names are independent — they need not match. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
88	
89	Check for existing solutions with `find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.uipx' -print` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` glob misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask the user which solution to use per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md) (rules #5 and #6): one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** last. Rule #5 owns the ask mechanism (structured `AskUserQuestion` where the runtime offers it, a numbered chat list otherwise, recommended-option fallback when non-interactive) — do not re-specify a tool here. Applies even when the user wants a new solution. If none are found, create a new one automatically.

94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.

111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.

113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. 139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. 145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {

152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"

156	  }

224	### Select the node type for each external service (runs even when full planning is skipped)
225	
226	Calling a named external service (Slack, open-meteo, Stripe, any REST API)? **Search first — never guess the node type from the brand name:**
227	
228	```bash
229	uip maestro flow registry search "<service>" --output json --output-filter "[*].{NodeType:NodeType,DisplayName:DisplayName,Description:Description,AvailableOnTenant:AvailableOnTenant}"
230	```
231	
232	Then pick the first match down this ladder:
233	
234	1. **Curated connector activity** (`uipath.connector.<key>.<op>` in the results) → use it.
235	2. **Connector exists but no activity for what you need** → `core.action.http.v2` (connector mode).
236	3. **No connector at all** → `core.action.http.v2` (manual mode).
237	4. **No API** (desktop app) → [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md).
238	
239	Manual HTTP is the **bottom of the ladder** — only the search returning no connector authorizes it. Picking it without searching is the brand-name shortcut forbidden by [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal).
240	
241	### Document-extraction step — route it to IxP (runs even when full planning is skipped)
242	
243	Pulling **named fields out of documents** (PDFs, scans, receipts, invoices, contracts, forms) is a document-extraction step — its node is an **IxP node** (`uipath.ixp.*`). It's easy to miss because the fetch/post steps around it are ordinary nodes, but the extraction in between is its own node. **Always land a node for it — never leave it out:**
244	
245	- **Model published** → land the real `uipath.ixp.*` node (skeleton is fine; defer config to Open Questions).
246	- **No model published** (`registry search "uipath.ixp"` → `Data: []`) → land a `core.logic.mock`.
247	
248	See [plugins/ixp/impl.md — Landing the node when you cannot fully configure it](plugins/ixp/impl.md#landing-the-node-when-you-cannot-fully-configure-it).
249	
250	**In-solution discovery (no login required):**
251	
252	```bash
253	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json     # discover sibling projects in the same .uipx solution
254	uip maestro flow registry search "<keyword>" --local --output json  # keyword search across in-solution nodes
255	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json  # get full manifest for a local node
256	```
257	
258	Run from inside the flow project directory. Returns the same manifest format as the tenant registry. Use `--local` to wire in-solution resources (RPA, agents, flows, API workflows) without publishing them first. `search --local` omits `AvailableOnTenant` — drop it from `--output-filter` projections.
259	
260	## Step 4 — Build the flow **[T2]**
261	
262	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:start-->
263	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
264	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:end-->
265	
266	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
267	
268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
270	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:end-->
271	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
272	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
273	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
274	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
275	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
276	
277	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
278	
279	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
280	
281	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
282	
283	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
284	
285	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
286	|---|---|---|
287	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
288	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
289	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
290	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
291	
292	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
293	
294	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
295	
296	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
297	
298	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
299	
300	**Or skip the anchoring problem:** `scripts/flow_edit.py` and `scripts/flow_compose.py` parse the file and rewrite the arrays directly, so no `old_string` has to be unique. One call per node, edge, variable, or composite rewrite — see [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) for the per-operation flags. `Edit` remains the right tool for a small in-place value change you want to show as a diff.
301	
302	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
303	
304	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).
305	
306	### Node ownership recap
307	
308	> **Before each node, classify it as user-owned or CLI-owned (see [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)). Connector activities, connector triggers, and `core.action.http.v2` are CLI-only — use `uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`, never Edit. Hand-writing these will fail `flow validate`.**
309	
310	Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` directly in the project root. The `bindings_v2.json` file is also in the project root for resource bindings.
311	
312	> **Tool selection by ownership.** Use `Edit` for in-place changes to user-owned nodes; `Write` only when ≥70% of nodes change **and the flow has no CLI-owned nodes** (a full-file `Write` over connector / managed-HTTP nodes clobbers their `bindings[]` — see the Step 4 `Write` note above). For CLI-owned nodes (above), use `uip maestro flow node add` + `node configure` — see the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for the full configuration workflow. Inline-agent project scaffolding uses `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`, but inline-agent flow node/wiring edits are direct `.flow` JSON (the agent node itself is user-owned).
313	
314	Read [editing-operations.md](editing-operations.md) for strategy selection and per-operation recipes.
315	
316	> **Self-check before each mutation:** name the tool you're about to use. If the answer isn't `Edit`, `Write`, or `uip maestro flow ...` — STOP and ask the user (per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). `python`, `node`, `jq`, `sed`, `awk`, and shell heredocs are a last resort and require explicit user approval after you've surfaced the trade-offs. See [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder).
317	
318	For each node type, follow the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for node-specific inputs, JSON structure, and configuration. The operations guides cover the mechanics (how to add/remove/wire); the plugins cover the semantics (what inputs and model fields each node type needs).
319	
320	## Step 5 — Validate **[T3 — chain with Step 6, plus any T1 `node configure`]**
321	
322	### Canonical T3 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
323	
324	```bash
325	uip maestro flow node configure "<ProjectName>.flow" "<httpNodeId>" --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>' --output json \
326	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
327	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json
328	```
329	
330	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). Tail-append one `node configure` per CLI-owned node added in T1, using the node IDs captured from T1's chained output. Drop the entire `node configure` segment if no CLI-owned nodes exist.
331	
332	> **The plugin `impl.md` is authoritative — follow its full procedure, not just its `--detail` schema, and let it override this turn map.** A plugin may prescribe steps the three-turn collapse does not show — most importantly a **pre-`configure` live fetch** whose output you must read before you can author `--detail` (the value depends on the live response, so it cannot be guessed or copied from a doc example). When `impl.md` defines such a step, run it in its **own turn before T3** and build `--detail` from its result; do not batch it into the chain, skip it, or hand-author the payload. An empty or static base response is expected for these steps and is not a signal the step is unavailable. This is general to every CLI-owned node type — defer to the owning `impl.md` rather than assuming static config.
333	
334	Chain `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py "<ProjectName>.flow"` into the same call, before `validate` — it reports the defects `validate` does not catch (wiring, `=js:` fields, Jint constructs, resource bindings, runtime gaps) while you are still in T3.
335	
336	**On validate failure:** one `Edit` turn to fix, then re-chain `validate && format` in one Bash. Do not validate after every individual Edit during T2 — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
337	
338	> **A passing exit code with warnings is NOT done.** `flow validate` returns 0 even when `Data.Warnings` is non-empty — read the warnings, don't just check the exit code. The connector-keyword warning (`node "…" mentions the "<connector>" connector keyword but uses the generic Managed HTTP type core.action.http.v2 with no connection binding`) means the flow took the brand-name shortcut and will run against an undefined endpoint at debug time — resolve it by switching to the connector before reporting the flow complete (see [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) and the anti-pattern list). Treat this class of warning as a build failure for your own definition of "done."
339	
340	### Common error categories
341	
342	- **Missing targetPort** — every edge needs a `targetPort` string
343	- **Missing definition** — every `type:typeVersion` in nodes needs a matching `definitions` entry
344	- **Invalid node/edge references** — `sourceNodeId`/`targetNodeId` must reference existing node `id`s
345	- **Duplicate IDs** — node and edge `id`s must be unique
346	
347	## Step 6 — Format node layout **[T3 — chained tail of Step 5]**
348	
349	This is the last segment of the [canonical T3 chain](#canonical-t3-chain--issue-this-as-one-bash-call) above. After validation passes, format must run before publishing or debugging (see "Always run `flow format` after edits" in [the Author capability index](../CAPABILITY.md)). Format:
350	
351	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) using ELK with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
352	- Sets each non-stickyNote node's `size` by its canvas shape so Studio Web renders it correctly: inline agents (`shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`, containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`, everything else (incl. referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>`) → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }` (skipping this leaves stale dimensions intact and produces misshapen nodes — the MST-9061 failure mode)
353	- Recurses into subflows and rewrites `subflows[<id>].layout`
354	- Backfills missing `position`/`size` entries
355	
356	Standalone (only if not chained from Step 5):
357	
358	```bash
359	uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow --output json
360	```
361	
362	## Completion Output
363	
364	When you finish building the flow, report to the user:
365	
366	1. **File path** of the `.flow` file created
367	2. **What was built** — summary of nodes added, edges wired, and logic implemented
368	3. **Validation status** — whether `flow validate` passes (or remaining errors if unresolvable)
369	4. **Format status** — confirm `flow format` was run
370	5. **Mock placeholders** — list any `core.logic.mock` nodes that need to be replaced, and which skill to use
371	6. **Missing connections** — any connector nodes that need connections the user must create
372	7. **What's next** — ask the user, presenting the dropdown below (see the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md))
373	
374	### What's next dropdown
375	
376	Authoring terminates here. Each option below hands off to Operate — read [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md) for the command sequence.
377	
378	| Option | What it does |
379	| --- | --- |
380	| **Publish to Studio Web** (default) | Push the solution to Studio Web so the user can visualize, edit, and publish from the browser. |
381	| **Debug the solution** | Execute the flow end-to-end against real systems. Confirm consent first — debug has real side effects (see the consent-before-debug rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). |
382	| **Deploy to Orchestrator** | Pack and publish directly to Orchestrator (bypasses Studio Web). Only when explicitly chosen — see [/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform). |
383	| **Something else** | Last option. Accept free-form string input and act on it (e.g., "just leave it", "pack but don't publish", "upload to a different tenant"). |
384	
385	Do not run any of these actions without explicit user selection. Once the user picks an option, read [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md) and follow that capability's flow — do not run operate commands from inside this doc.

1	# Connections
2	
3	Connections are authenticated sessions for a specific connector. They store credentials and tokens, and can be shared across automations within a folder.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Response Fields
10	
11	| Field | Show to user? | Description |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| **`Name`** | **Yes** | Display name — always use this as the primary identifier when presenting to the user (e.g., "Salesforce Prod", "bai.li") |
14	| **`State`** | **Yes** | `Enabled` or other status. Only Enabled connections can be used. |
15	| **`IsDefault`** | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. Recommend the default connection but always let the user confirm. |
16	| **`Owner`** | **Yes** | Who created the connection (email) |
17	| **`Folder`** | **Yes** | Folder name this connection belongs to (e.g., "Shared", "Personal") |
18	| `ConnectorName` | **Yes** | Human-readable connector name (e.g., "Slack", "Salesforce") |
19	| `ByoaConnection` | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connection — customer registered their own OAuth app with the external service. Required for some webhook triggers. |
20	| `Id` | Internal | Connection UUID — use only in `--connection-id` CLI args, never show to user |
21	| `ConnectorKey` | Internal | Connector key — use only in CLI args |
22	| `FolderKey` | Internal | Folder UUID — use only in `--folder-key` CLI args, never show to user |
23	| `ElementInstanceId` | Internal | Numeric instance ID — use only in `--element-instance-id` for `uip is webhooks config` |
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Command Syntax
28	
29	`<connector-key>` is a **positional argument**, not a flag:
30	
31	```bash
32	# Correct — always pass --all-folders for discovery (see Folder Scoping below)
33	uip is connections list "uipath-salesforce-slack" --all-folders --output json
34	
35	# WRONG — there is no --connector-key flag
36	uip is connections list --connector-key "uipath-salesforce-slack"
37	```
38	
39	**Always pass a connector key.** Running `uip is connections list` with no arg returns a noisy, paginated list across every connector in the tenant and is not a useful survey step.
40	
41	**Wrong key?** If the call errors with "connector not found" or returns empty unexpectedly, look up the correct key:
42	
43	```bash
44	uip is connectors list --filter "<vendor>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	Connector keys are prefixed by source — `uipath-<vendor>-<service>` for catalog connectors, `custom-entity-*` for tenant-built. See [connectors.md — Connector Disambiguation](connectors.md#connector-disambiguation) for the full classification ladder.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Selecting a Connection
52	
53	### Connector-Specific Overrides
54	
55	**Before applying the auto-select rule below, check this table.** If the connector key (and node-type pattern, where listed) matches an entry, read the linked file and follow its rules. Override supersedes the auto-select rule.
56	
57	| Connector key | Applies when | Override action | Detail |
58	|---|---|---|---|
59	| `uipath-microsoft-teams` | `send-bot-*` activity node types | Ask user; warn that bot scope is required | [uipath-microsoft-teams.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-microsoft-teams.md#connection-selection-override) |
60	| `uipath-salesforce-slack` | Webhook trigger node types (allow-list — excludes `button-clicked`) | Ask user; filter `--byoa` from the start | [uipath-salesforce-slack.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-salesforce-slack.md#connection-selection-override) |
61	
62	To add a new override, see [connector-overrides/README.md](connector-overrides/README.md).
63	
64	---
65	
66	**Auto-select rule (no prompt) — when all three hold:**
67	
68	- `IsDefault: Yes`
69	- `State: Enabled`
70	- `Folder` is the user's personal workspace
71	
72	Bind silently and skip the presentation steps below.
73	
74	Detect the user's personal workspace once per session — list all folders and filter for the personal type:
75	
76	```bash
77	uip or folders list --all --output json
78	# → Data: [{ Name, Key, Path, Description, Type, ParentKey }]
79	# Filter entries where Type == "Personal"
80	```
81	
82	Match `connection.FolderKey` against the personal workspace's `Key`. If the call returns multiple personal workspaces (admin tenant) or no match, fall through to the presentation flow.
83	
84	**Otherwise — present connections to the user.** Recommend the default but let the user confirm.
85	
86	### Folder Scoping (`--all-folders`)
87	
88	**Always pass `--all-folders` when discovering connections.** Without it, the CLI returns the active folder only — producing false "no connections found" results when the connection exists in another folder you can see. After the user picks a connection, capture its `FolderKey` from the response for downstream binding; do not pass `--folder-key` during discovery.
89	
90	- `--all-folders`: spans every folder you have access to. Works with or without a `<connector-key>` positional.
91	- **Mutually exclusive with `--folder` / `--folder-key`** — passing both fails with `Result: Failure`, `Message: "Conflicting folder flags..."`, exit code 1.
92	
93	### For Native Connectors
94	
95	1. List connections for the connector across all folders:
96	
97	   ```bash
98	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
99	   ```
100	
101	2. Present all enabled connections to the user using **Name, Owner, and Folder** (never UUIDs), **recommending** the default (`IsDefault: Yes`, `State: Enabled`):
102	   - "I found these connections: 1) **Salesforce Prod** by user@example.com (default, enabled, Shared folder) ← recommended 2) **Salesforce Dev** by admin@example.com (enabled, Shared folder). Which should I use?"
103	3. If only one enabled connection exists, still confirm: "I found connection **<Name>** by <Owner> in **<Folder>** folder (default, enabled). Should I use this one?"
104	4. **Verify health — ping after every selection** (auto-select and user-confirmed alike):
105	
106	   ```bash
107	   uip is connections ping "<connection-id>" --output json
108	   ```
109	
110	   If ping fails or reports not Enabled, follow step 5.
111	
112	5. If not enabled (from list `State` or ping result) → prompt user to re-authenticate via `is connections edit <id>`, then re-ping.
113	
114	6. **No connections in step 1 — bypass the cache before concluding none exist:**
115	   1. Retry with `--refresh`:
116	      ```bash
117	      uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --refresh --output json
118	      ```
119	   2. If still empty, prompt user to create one via `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`.
120	
121	### For BYOA Connections (Webhook Triggers)
122	
123	BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connections use an OAuth app the customer registered with the external service (e.g., a Slack app they own). Some webhook triggers require BYOA; many do not. **The requirement is per event object, not per connector** — read it from the `triggers objects` response.
124	
125	**Decision flow:**
126	
127	1. Get any enabled connection — needed only as `--connection-id` for the next call:
128	
129	   ```bash
130	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
131	   ```
132	
133	2. Query trigger objects and read the `byoaConnection` flag for the matching event:
134	
135	   ```bash
136	   uip is triggers objects "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" \
137	     --connection-id "<id>" --output json
138	   ```
139	
140	3. **If `byoaConnection: true`** — the connection from step 1 is not usable. Filter to BYOA across all folders:
141	
142	   ```bash
143	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --output json
144	   ```
145	
146	   If empty, retry with `--refresh` to bypass the CLI cache:
147	
148	   ```bash
149	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --refresh --output json
150	   ```
151	
152	   If still empty, **stop and tell the user**: "This trigger requires a BYOA connection for `<connector-key>`. None found. Create one in the Integration Service portal or with `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`, then re-run."
153	
154	4. **If `byoaConnection: false`** — use the connection from step 1. Verify health with `uip is connections ping "<id>" --output json`.
155	
156	> Connector-specific OAuth-app setup instructions (e.g., what permissions a Slack app needs) come from the trigger's `design.textBlocks` field in the `triggers objects` response. Surface that text to the user verbatim — do not invent service-specific guidance.
157	
158	For webhook URL retrieval after the trigger is configured, see [triggers.md — Webhook URL Retrieval](triggers.md#webhook-url-retrieval).
159	
160	### For HTTP Fallback
161	
162	1. List connections for `uipath-uipath-http`
163	2. Look for a connection whose **Name** contains the target vendor (case-insensitive substring match, e.g., "Apify" matches "Apify", "Apify - Prod", "My Apify Connection")
164	3. Present matches to the user. If multiple matches → let them choose.
165	4. If no match → present all existing HTTP connections and ask the user to choose, or offer to create a new one
166	
167	> **Note:** Name-based matching is best-effort. If connection names don't follow vendor naming conventions, present all HTTP connections to the user.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Folder Scoping
172	
173	`uip is connections list <connector-key>` defaults to filtering by the **current** folder context — results from other folders (including the user's personal workspace) are silently excluded. Empty response on the filtered side looks like:
174	
175	```json
176	{"Message":"No connections found for connector '<connector-key>'."}
177	```
178	
179	even though a connection exists in another folder.
180	
181	**Cross-folder pattern** — pass `--folder` explicitly:
182	
183	```bash
184	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
185	```
186	
187	**Enumerate every folder** — iterate folders and list per folder:
188	
189	```bash
190	uip or folders list --output json
191	# → for each folder, call:
192	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
193	```
194	
195	> If the user reports "connection exists in my personal workspace but CLI can't see it", suspect default folder filtering — re-list with `--folder` set to that workspace before creating a new connection.
196	
197	---
198	
199	## Identifying a JDBC Connection's Target DB
200	
201	For the JDBC gateway connector (`uipath-uipath-jdbc`, "Database Hub"), `connections list` does **not** expose `jdbcUrl` or `driverClass` — config is intentionally hidden. The only signal for "what DB does this JDBC connection point to?" is the connection **`name`**.
202	
203	Match case-insensitively (weak signal — surface as "likely <DB>", never "is <DB>"):
204	
205	| DB | Substrings in `connection.name` |
206	|---|---|
207	| Snowflake | `snowflake`, `sf` |
208	| Databricks | `databricks`, `dbx` |
209	| Postgres | `postgres`, `postgresql`, `pg` |
210	| MySQL | `mysql` |
211	| SQL Server | `sqlserver`, `mssql` |
212	| Oracle | `oracle` |
213	| Redshift | `redshift` |
214	| BigQuery | `bigquery`, `bq` |
215	
216	If the user explicitly named a connection in their prompt (e.g. "use the `pat_databricks` connection"), that overrides name-matching — bind it directly.
217	
218	Used by the [connectors.md — JDBC Gateway](connectors.md#jdbc-gateway--database-sql-intent) decision matrix.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## Getting a Connection's Vendor Base URL
223	
224	`uip is connections base-url <connection-id>` returns the exact vendor base URL the connection uses for proxied calls (e.g., raw `http-request` calls, Managed HTTP Request in connector mode). Manual-mode invocations don't use it. The connection must be Enabled.
225	
226	```bash
227	uip is connections base-url "<connection-id>" --output json
228	# → { "Result": "Success", "Code": "ConnectionBaseUrl",
229	#     "Data": { "ConnectionId": "<id>", "BaseUrl": "https://..." } }
230	```
231	
232	Examples across connectors:
233	
234	| Connector | Returned `BaseUrl` |
235	|---|---|
236	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<site-id>/rest/api/2` |
237	| `uipath-microsoft-outlook365` | `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0` |
238	| `uipath-uipath-marketo` | `https://<account>.mktorest.com/rest` |
239	
240	Use this whenever you need to compose a relative `url` for `http-request` or Managed HTTP Request in connector mode. See [http-request.md](http-request.md).
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Scope-Related Errors
245	
246	A connection can be `Enabled` but lack optional OAuth scopes needed for specific activities. This typically surfaces as a **403 Forbidden** error during execute.
247	
248	**Symptoms:**
249	- Connection pings successfully (`State: Enabled`)
250	- Execute fails with 403 or a vendor-specific "insufficient permissions" error
251	- The same operation works with a different connection that has broader scopes
252	
253	**Recovery:**
254	1. Inform the user that the connection may need broader OAuth scopes for this activity
255	2. Re-authorize with broader scopes: `uip is connections edit <connection-id>`
256	3. After re-auth, ping again to verify, then retry the operation

1	# Resources
2	
3	Resources represent the data objects available through a connector (e.g., Salesforce Account, Contact, Opportunity). Each resource supports a set of CRUD operations.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	## Contents
8	- Listing and Describing Resources
9	- Response Fields
10	- Describe Response
11	- Describe Failures
12	- Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
13	- Execute Operations
14	- Pagination
15	- Execute Error Handling
16	
17	For reference field resolution (simple refs, dependency chains, required field validation), see [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md).
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Listing and Describing Resources
22	
23	**Always pass `--connection-id`** to get connection-specific metadata including custom objects and fields. Without it, only standard objects/fields are returned.
24	
25	## Response Fields
26	
27	| Field | Description |
28	|---|---|
29	| **`Name`** | Resource identifier (used in commands) |
30	| `DisplayName` | Human-readable name |
31	| `Path` | API path for this resource |
32	| `Type` | Resource type (standard, custom) |
33	| `SubType` | Sub-type (e.g., method, entity) |
34	
35	## Describe Response
36	
37	The describe command returns metadata from the raw API. The output depends on whether `--operation` is provided.
38	
39	### Without `--operation` — operation summary
40	
41	Returns which operations the resource supports:
42	
43	| Field | Description |
44	|---|---|
45	| **`availableOperations`** | List of operations — each with `method` (GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE), `name` (Create/List/etc.), `description`, `curated` (display name) |
46	| **`hint`** | Instructs to use `--operation` for field details |
47	
48	### With `--operation` — per-operation field detail
49	
50	Returns the full field breakdown for the specified operation:
51	
52	| Field | Description |
53	|---|---|
54	| **`operation`** | Operation info — `method`, `name`, `description`, `path`, `curated` display name |
55	| **`parameters`** | Path and query parameters (NOT body fields) — each with `name`, `type` (path/query), `dataType`, `required`, `defaultValue`, `reference` |
56	| **`requestFields`** | Fields to send in `--body` — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName`, `required`, `description`, `reference`, `enum` |
57	| **`responseFields`** | Fields returned in the response — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName` |
58	
59	> **Always use `--operation`** to get actionable field detail. Without it you only see which operations exist.
60	
61	### Key field properties
62	
63	- **`required: true`** — field must be provided in `--body` or `--query`. Do NOT skip.
64	- **`reference`** — field value must be looked up from another resource. See [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md). When baking a static value for a reference field, also emit `designTimeMetadata.designTimeLookups` so the edit-UI renders a label — see [reference-resolution.md — Static Reference-Value Labeling](reference-resolution.md#static-reference-value-labeling).
65	- **`enum`** — field only accepts the listed values (e.g., `["low", "normal", "high"]`).
66	
67	Results are cached locally. Use `--refresh` to bypass cache after re-auth or schema changes.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Describe Failures
72	
73	Some resources return an error on describe. This is a **server-side metadata gap** — do not retry with `--refresh`.
74	
75	**Recovery:**
76	
77	1. **Skip describe entirely** — do not waste calls retrying.
78	2. **Infer fields from user context** — use the field names and values the user provided in their request.
79	3. **Infer reference fields from naming** — see [reference-resolution.md — Inferring References Without Describe](reference-resolution.md#inferring-references-without-describe).
80	4. **Attempt execute directly** — let the server validate. If a field is rejected, read the error and adjust.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
85	
86	For connectors whose required fields depend on parent-field selections (Jira `GenerateSchema` keyed off project + issue type, Salesforce SOQL `GenerateQuerySchema` keyed off the query string, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant` keyed off `tenantEntityName`), the base `describe` returns only base fields. To preview the full required-field set the runtime will see, pass parent values via `-f, --field`:
87	
88	```bash
89	# Jira: project + issue type → custom fields (GET, query-param tokens)
90	uip is resources describe uipath-atlassian-jira curated_create_issue \
91	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
92	  -f fields.project.key=ENGCE \
93	  -f fields.issuetype.id=3 \
94	  --output json
95	
96	# Salesforce SOQL: query string → response columns (POST, body token)
97	uip is resources describe uipath-salesforce-sfdc query_records \
98	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
99	  -f query="SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Status = 'Active'" \
100	  --output json
101	```
102	
103	What it does — runs the matching api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service (same path Studio Web's dispatcher uses), then merges the response into `requestFields` per the action's `onSuccess.remapConfiguration`. Use it before validating required fields to catch project- or operation-specific mandatory fields the base describe can't see.
104	
105	| Flag | Notes |
106	|------|-------|
107	| `-f, --field <name=value>` | Repeatable. Token names match `apiConfiguration.url` and `apiConfiguration.body` placeholders verbatim — no `_sub_` encoding (encoding only applies when caching parent values for runtime replay; see [activities.md — Custom Fields](activities.md#custom-fields-objectactionsactiontypeapi)). |
108	| `--action <name>` | Optional. Disambiguates when more than one api-type action could match the field set. |
109	
110	Requires `--connection-id` and `--operation`. Cache is bypassed when `--field` is supplied — the action response varies per parent-field combination. The merge mode (`replace` / `append` / `prepend` / `noop`) comes from the action's `remapConfiguration.input`; for Jira `GenerateSchema` it is `replace`.
111	
112	When no api-type action's `rules[]` are satisfied by the supplied fields, the CLI errors with `No api-type ObjectAction matched for fields [...]`. List the operation's actions from the describe output's `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (or top-level `objectActions[]` for older shapes) to see which fields each action requires.
113	
114	---
115	
116	## Execute Operations
117	
118	| Verb | Description | `--body` | `--query` |
119	|---|---|---|---|
120	| `create` | Create a new record | Yes | No |
121	| `list` | Retrieve multiple records | No | Optional (`limit=10&offset=0`) |
122	| `get` | Get a single record by ID | No | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
123	| `update` | Partial update (PATCH) | Yes | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
124	| `delete` | Delete a record | No | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
125	| `replace` | Full replacement (PUT) | Yes | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
126	
127	> **Update** (PATCH) = change specific fields. **Replace** (PUT) = overwrite entire record. Default to **Update** unless the user says "replace" or "overwrite".
128	
129	### Filtering Results with `--output-filter`
130	
131	Use the global `--output-filter` flag with a JMESPath expression to extract specific fields from large responses if possible via JMESPath.
132	
133	```bash
134	# Extract only id, name, and email from a user list
135	uip is resources execute list "<CONNECTOR_KEY>" "<OBJECT_NAME>" \
136	  --connection-id "<CONNECTION_ID>" \
137	  --output json \
138	  --output-filter "Data[].{id: id, name: name, email: profile.email}"
139	```
140	
141	Common JMESPath patterns:
142	
143	| Pattern | Effect |
144	|---|---|
145	| `Data[]` | Return all records (unwrap the Data envelope) |
146	| `Data[].name` | Return just the `name` field from each record |
147	| `Data[].{id: id, name: name}` | Return selected fields as objects |
148	| `Data[?status=='active']` | Filter records by field value |
149	| `Data[0]` | Return only the first record |
150	
151	---
152	
153	## Pagination
154	
155	`uip is resources execute list` may not return all results in a single call. **Always check for pagination** when searching for a specific item or listing all items.
156	
157	### Pagination rules
158	
159	1. **Always check `Data.Pagination`** — every `list` response may contain pagination state. Never assume a single page contains all results.
160	2. **Complete the pagination loop** — when searching for a specific item, keep paginating until `Data.Pagination.HasMore` is `"false"` or the item is found. Do NOT abandon pagination mid-loop to try alternative APIs (e.g., search endpoints, admin endpoints, HTTP fallback).
161	3. **Stop early on match** — if you find the target item in the current page, stop. No need to fetch remaining pages.
162	4. **Report not-found only after exhausting all pages** — only conclude an item does not exist after `HasMore` is `"false"` and every page has been checked.
163	
164	### Connector pagination
165	
166	Most IS connectors use the `elements-*` pagination protocol. The CLI returns pagination state nested inside `Data.Pagination`:
167	
168	- **`Data.Pagination.HasMore`**: `"true"` or `"false"` — indicates if more pages exist
169	- **`Data.Pagination.NextPageToken`**: the token value to use for the next page
170	
171	**IMPORTANT:** The query parameter name is `nextPage` (NOT `nextPageToken`). Pass the value from `Data.Pagination.NextPageToken` as `--query "nextPage=<value>"`.
172	
173	```bash
174	# First page (do not pass pageSize unless the user explicitly requests a specific page size)
175	uip is resources execute list "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
176	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
177	# → Check Data.Pagination.HasMore and Data.Pagination.NextPageToken in the JSON response
178	
179	# Subsequent pages — use nextPage as the query param name (NOT nextPageToken)
180	uip is resources execute list "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
181	  --connection-id "<id>" --query "nextPage=<value-from-NextPageToken>" --output json
182	# → Continue until Data.Pagination.HasMore is "false" or target item is found
183	```
184	
185	Example response:
186	```json
187	{
188	  "Result": "Success",
189	  "Code": "ExecuteOperation",
190	  "Data": {
191	    "items": [ ... ],
192	    "Pagination": {
193	      "HasMore": "true",
194	      "NextPageToken": "eyJwYWdl..."
195	    }
196	  }
197	}
198	```
199	
200	### Anti-patterns
201	
202	- **Do NOT check `Data.nextPage`** — pagination lives at `Data.Pagination.HasMore` and `Data.Pagination.NextPageToken`, not at `Data.nextPage`.
203	- **Do NOT abandon pagination to try other APIs** — if you are paginating through `conversations` to find a channel, do not stop mid-loop to call `admin_conversations_search`, `search_all`, or `search_messages`. Complete the loop first.
204	- **Do NOT conclude "not found" after one page** — a single page may return only a fraction of the total results. Always check `Data.Pagination.HasMore` before concluding.
205	
206	### Query-param pagination (offset/limit)
207	
208	Some resources support `offset`/`limit` via `--query`:
209	
210	```bash
211	uip is resources execute list "<connector-key>" "<object>" \
212	  --connection-id "<id>" --query "limit=50&offset=0" --output json
213	# → next page: --query "limit=50&offset=50"
214	```
215	
216	Stop when the result set is empty or smaller than the limit.
217	
218	### HTTP connector exception
219	
220	Connectors with key `uipath-uipath-http` do NOT use the `elements-*` pagination headers. These depend on vendor-specific pagination. Handle on a case-by-case basis.
221	
222	---
223	
224	## Execute Error Handling
225	
226	When an execute command fails, the CLI returns:
227	- **`Message`**: HTTP status (e.g., `400 Bad Request`)
228	- **`Instructions`**: The raw vendor error response body as JSON
229	
230	### How to diagnose failures
231	
232	1. **Read `Message`** — the HTTP status code tells you the category (400 = bad request, 403 = forbidden, 404 = not found, etc.)
233	2. **Read `Instructions`** — the raw vendor error body tells you WHAT specifically failed (invalid field, missing required value, permission denied, etc.)
234	3. **Use discovery to fix** — run `describe` to get valid field names, run `list` to get valid values for reference fields
235	4. **Retry with fixes** — apply the specific correction and re-execute (max 2 retries)
236	
237	For the full recovery loop, see [agent-workflow.md — Error Recovery](agent-workflow.md#error-recovery).

1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (generated scaffold)](#project-structure-generated-scaffold)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
52	
53	## Project structure (generated scaffold)
54	
55	```
56	<ProjectName>/
57	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
58	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
59	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
60	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
61	├── operate.json            # runtime options
62	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
63	```
64	
65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
119	
120	Example — manual start trigger:
121	
122	```json
123	{
124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
191	
192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — without rewriting anything; `uip maestro flow format` remains the fix.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
229	
230	## Edge — both ports required
231	
232	```json
233	{
234	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
235	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
236	  "sourcePort": "output",
237	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
238	  "targetPort": "input"
239	}
240	```
241	
242	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
245	>
246	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.
247	
248	## Definition entry
249	
250	Every node type appearing in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`. Get the correct definition from:
251	
252	```bash
253	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
254	```
255	
256	Copy the returned node definition object into your `definitions` array. Depending on CLI/plugin version, that object may appear at `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`. Do not write definitions by hand — always pull from the registry to ensure schema compliance.
257	
258	## Common node types
259	
260	| Type | Purpose | Key inputs |
261	|------|---------|------------|
262	| `core.trigger.manual` | Entry point | `entryPointId` |
263	| `core.trigger.scheduled` | Recurring schedule trigger | `entryPointId`, `timerType`, `timerPreset` |
264	| `core.action.script` | Run JavaScript | `script` |
265	| `core.action.http.v2` | HTTP request | `method`, `url`, `headers`, `body` |
266	| `core.action.transform` | Map/filter/group data | `collection`, `operations` |
267	| `core.logic.decision` | If/else branch | `expression` |
268	| `core.logic.switch` | Multi-way branch | `cases` |
269	| `core.logic.loop` | Iterate collection | `collection`, `parallel` |
270	| `core.logic.merge` | Sync parallel paths | — |
271	| `core.control.end` | Graceful end | — |
272	| `core.logic.terminate` | Abort workflow | — |
273	
274	> The BPMN type for each node (e.g., `bpmn:StartEvent`, `bpmn:ScriptTask`) lives in the `definitions` entry copied from `uip maestro flow registry get`. Instances do not carry the BPMN type.
275	
276	For full details on each node (ports, inputs, outputs, when to use), see the [Author planning architecture guide](../author/references/planning-arch.md). For implementation resolution (registry lookups, connection binding, reference field resolution), see the [Author planning implementation guide](../author/references/planning-impl.md).
277	
278	Discover all available types:
279	```bash
280	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
281	uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>
282	```
283	
284	## Standard ports by node type
285	
286	| Node type | Source ports (outgoing) | Target ports (incoming) |
287	|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
288	| `core.trigger.manual` | `output` | — |
289	| `core.action.script` | `success`, `error` | `input` |
290	| `core.action.http.v2` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic) | `input` |
291	| `core.action.transform` | `output`, `error` | `input` |
292	| `core.logic.decision` | `true`, `false` | `input` |
293	| `core.logic.switch` | `case-{id}` (dynamic), `default` | `input` |
294	| `core.logic.loop` | `success`, `output` | `input`, `loopBack` |
295	| `core.logic.merge` | `output` | `input` |
296	| `core.control.end` | — | `input` |
297	| `core.logic.terminate` | — | `input` |
298	
299	Connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes follow the same pattern as the generic action nodes above: a primary source port plus an implicit `error` port.
300	
301	Verify exact ports for any node type:
302	```bash
303	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
